Intermodal leads weekly gains as US rail traffic rises 3.5%, says AAR
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic increased 3.5% in the week ending Oct. 31 compared with the same week in 2025, the Association of American Railroads said Wednesday. Carload traffic rose 3.0%, while intermodal volume increased 3.9%. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded year-over-year gains. Metallic ores and metals led with an 18.3% increase, followed by forest products at 9.3% and motor vehicles and parts at 9.1%. Chemicals rose 7.9%, farm products excluding grain and food increased 6.9%, petroleum and petroleum products gained 2.5%, and nonmetallic minerals edged up 1.1%. Miscellaneous carloads posted the largest weekly decline, falling 12.2%. Grain traffic dropped 8.3%, while coal slipped 0.4%. For the first 43 weeks of 2026, total U.S. rail traffic increased 3.8% from the same period last year. Intermodal volume rose 4.7%, outpacing a 2.7% gain in carloads. candidates.title: Port of Gothenburg reports stable freight flows
candidates.excerpt: Cargo volumes at the Port of Gothenburg developed steadily from January to September 2026. Container volumes were in line with the previous year, while several segments grew clearly: new cars rose 14% and energy products 10%, and Ro/Ro traffic and rail volumes also continued to increase. The port handled 698,000 TEU in the period, against 699,000 TEU a year earlier. Behind the largely unchanged total lies a 2% rise in laden containers and an 11% fall in empty container handling, meaning more cargo and less air than before. Imports of laden containers increased 7%, while exports decreased 1%. Around 60 percent of containers are moved by rail to or from the hinterland. Rail volumes reached 403,000 TEU, up 2 percent on the same period last year, which puts rail traffic on course for another record year. candidates.title: Transpacific emerges as liner shipping’s golden trade
candidates.excerpt: The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope. New analysis from Alphaliner shows that the extraordinary strength of the US trade has persisted well beyond the traditional peak season, with freight rates approaching levels last seen during the pandemic. At approximately $7,500 per feu, the 5,775 nautical mile Shanghai–Los Angeles voyage generates $1.30 in revenue per container per nautical mile, compared with just 26 cents on Shanghai–Rotterdam via the Cape, or 34 cents via Suez. Shanghai–New York generates 96 cents per nautical mile, with spot rates remaining above $10,000 per feu since late August. candidates.excerpt: Funding Circle appoints Rob Straathof as CEO UK small business lender Funding Circle has appointed former Liberis boss Rob Straathof as its next chief executive. Straathof succeeds Lisa Jacobs, who announced in September that she was stepping down from the role. He will join Funding Circle in the first half of 2027, with Jacobs continuing to lead the business in the meantime before departing no later than September 2027.
